investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-16T00:59 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every attempt. Because all three sibling checks share the identical error message and all failed within the same ~33-second window, the failure is localized to the shared upstream swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-detected infrastructure availability signal, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The AWS ELB serving the swarm /v1/agents endpoint was unhealthy, stopped, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — causing the production-api to receive a connection error and surface it as 502 bad_gateway.

[Possible] A network routing or security-group change in us-east-2 severed connectivity between the production-api and the swarm ELB, making the endpoint unreachable without the ELB itself being down.
[Possible] The swarm service behind the ELB was restarting or had crashed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy targets and returning 502 to all inbound requests.
[Less likely] A transient network blip in us-east-2 caused a brief but complete loss of connectivity to the ELB during the ~33-second eval window; the service may have self-recovered.

[Cannot assess without additional evidence] A deployment or configuration change to the swarm service or its ELB listener rules may have caused the gateway to become unreachable; no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) with a valid vmId and remoteState at or near the same timestamp would disprove gateway unavailability.

ELB access logs showing healthy 2xx responses to /v1/agents requests during the 2026-09-16T00:59:01–00:59:34Z window would indicate the failure is in the production-api routing layer rather than the ELB itself.
A passing re-run of the remote-agent-create eval immediately after the failure window would suggest a transient blip rather than a sustained gateway outage.
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed, the root cause would be localized to check-specific logic rather than the shared swarm gateway.

Evidence that the ELB was healthy and accepting traffic during the failure window would shift the hypothesis toward a production-api misconfiguration or credential/auth failure on the outbound request.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create on a shorter interval (e.g., every 5 minutes) to reduce mean-time-to-detect for swarm gateway outages.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-16T00:59 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every attempt. Because all three sibling checks share the identical error message and all failed within the same ~33-second window, the failure is localized to the shared upstream swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-detected infrastructure availability signal, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The AWS ELB serving the swarm /v1/agents endpoint was unhealthy, stopped, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — causing the production-api to receive a connection error and surface it as 502 bad_gateway.

[Possible] A network routing or security-group change in us-east-2 severed connectivity between the production-api and the swarm ELB, making the endpoint unreachable without the ELB itself being down.
[Possible] The swarm service behind the ELB was restarting or had crashed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy targets and returning 502 to all inbound requests.
[Less likely] A transient network blip in us-east-2 caused a brief but complete loss of connectivity to the ELB during the ~33-second eval window; the service may have self-recovered.

[Cannot assess without additional evidence] A deployment or configuration change to the swarm service or its ELB listener rules may have caused the gateway to become unreachable; no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a manual POST /api/agents call with a valid token succeeds and returns a 200 with agent identity fields, the gateway was not broadly down and the failure may be eval-runner-specific (e.g., credential or network egress issue from the CI environment).
If only the remote-agents checks fail but local-agent-create or other agent checks pass, the issue is isolated to the swarm/remote provisioning path rather than a general API outage.
If the ELB target group shows all targets healthy and no 5xx errors in CloudWatch during the 2026-09-16T00:59 window, the 502 may have been a transient blip rather than a sustained gateway failure.
If the eval run history (currently empty: previousRunCount=0) shows this check was never passing, the gateway may have been misconfigured from the start rather than having regressed.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that directly probes the ELB /v1/agents endpoint (or a health check path) and asserts a non-5xx response, so gateway failures are caught before the full agent provisioning flow is attempted.

Add a gateway-reachability pre-check that runs before remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime, so a shared gateway failure is surfaced as a single root-cause signal rather than three separate check failures.
Add eval run history retention so that lastPassingAt and previousStatuses are populated, enabling regression detection (currentlyRegressedFromPass) for future gateway failures.
Consider adding a latency-only probe for POST /api/agents that asserts a non-502 response within the warningLatencyMs threshold, to catch partial gateway degradation before a full 502 outage.
